research_period: Milan, Paris and Pitti Uomo menswear shows, June 2026; Premiere Vision Paris, February 2026; analysis July to November 2026
markets: Global: Milan, Paris and Florence runways; premium and mid-market menswear
title: SS27 Men's Assortment and Pricing Strategy
summary: Plan SS27 menswear for low growth: separates and sets that combine, summer tailoring sold as separates, shallow fashion buys and full price on what is new.

sections.heading: The market
sections.body: Fashion is expected to remain in low single-digit growth in 2027; sales up 4% with inventory up 10% is a weaker position than steady stock; mid-market brands face promotional pressure from luxury and value players<sup>[1]</sup>. Resale is expected to grow two to three times faster than first-hand fashion through 2027<sup>[1]</sup>.

sections.heading: Assortment
sections.body:
| Tier | What goes in it |
|---|---|
| Core (about half) | Shirts in ice blue and white, straight trousers, knit polos, sand and tobacco |
| Seasonal (about a third) | Summer suits, shorts, cropped blousons, sets, satin shirts |
| Statement (the rest) | Studded denim, sheer shirts, skirts and aprons, orange and aquatic pieces |

sections.heading: Pricing
sections.body:
- Full price on rising pieces (cropped jackets, summer suits, sets).
- Value on core reorder lines.
- Premium for leather and hand-finished pieces.
- Sets priced to reward buying both pieces.

design_implications: - Fewer styles, more combinations; shared fabrics across shirts and sets.
commercial_implications:
- Weekly sales-to-stock tracking; chase winners.
- In the EU, plan rework and resale routes for unsold stock.

sources.title: Fashion: 2027, the year growth will finally have to be profitable
